question.text: The half life period of a radioactive element <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is same as the mean life time of another radioactive element <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Initially they have the same number of atoms. Then:

options.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> decay at the same rate always.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> have same decay rate initially and later on different decay rate.

solution.text:
The formula of half-life in terms of the decay constant, t12=0.693λx=1λy
⇒λx=0.693λy⇒ λx<λy
